finding.claim: SQL injection in /search: the q query parameter is interpolated directly into the SQL string via an f-string, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to alter the query (e.g. UNION SELECT to read any table in shop.db, including columns not exposed by the endpoint).
finding.source: request.args.get('q') on GET /search (app.py:11), fully attacker-controlled, no authentication
finding.sink: db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'") at app.py:12

trace.note: term = request.args.get('q', '') taken from the query string with no validation
term embedded in SQL via f-string rather than a bound parameter
query results returned to the caller as JSON, so injected UNION output is exfiltrated

finding.guards_checked: No input validation, escaping, parameterization, authentication, or WAF present in the file. The other two queries (lines 18, 25) use ? placeholders, confirming this one is the outlier. sqlite3 execute() blocks stacked statements, so impact is limited to read/exfiltration via UNION/boolean/error techniques rather than stacked writes.

verdict.reason: app.py:11 reads q from the query string unvalidated, app.py:12 interpolates it into the SQL via an f-string, and app.py:13 returns the rows as JSON; the route has no authentication, and the only parameterized queries are the other routes (app.py:18, 25).
